title: What Is Agent Visibility?
summary: AI agent visibility is knowing which agents operate in an environment, what access they hold, and what they actually did. The three evidence sources behind it, and why it is not brand visibility in AI search.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


**AI agent visibility is the ability to identify the agents operating in an environment, understand the access available to them, and inspect evidence of their actions. Discovery, authorization records and activity logs provide different parts of that picture.**


Those three parts come from three different places, and most enterprises have one of them. Discovery answers which agents exist. Authorization records answer what each one could do. Activity logs answer what it did, for whom, and with what result. Any single source read alone will mislead you.


The common framing is that a catalogue plus an agent inventory gets you most of the way. In our reading of how these programmes actually fail, it does not. An inventory entry saying "read access to the supplier database" is a claim about permission, and the space between a permission and its use only appears if something is recording activity.


One naming collision is worth clearing up first, because it sends a lot of search traffic to the wrong page: "agent visibility" in the marketing sense means how often an AI assistant mentions your brand. That is not this. This is the security and operations question about software agents inside your own systems.


Today: emit` invoke_agent` and` execute_tool` spans with the agent, the acting user and the tool on every call, leave content capture off by default, and write down which attribute names your dashboards read.
